Winter of the Twenty-fourth Year of Beihong," with an inscription of "Xu Beihong" in white characters.　　The twenty-fourth year refers to the twenty-fourth year of the Republic of China (1935), when Xu Beihong was 40 years old.　　This painting is inscribed by Shang Chengjo at the poetry pond: "A chicken has five virtues, one of which is charity. Assembling three chicks, the legacy of love of the great thousands. The Buddha's cloud is, and the bodhi phase is. Mahayana Chan Duer painter, creation and transformation Bi Xuan. Inscribed by Shang Chengjo in the twelfth month of the twelfth lunar month." Inscription of "Shang" in white and "Zhai" in vermilion. "Kuiwei" means 1943, eight years after Xu Beihong created this picture.　　This picture is an idyllic painting, the chicks are foraging for food under the guidance of the hen, simple motherly affection overflowing in the brush. Xu Beihong has created many paintings with chickens as the theme, but it is not common to see paintings with hens and chicks as the subject matter.　　The artist uses different brushwork to represent the hen and the chick: the hen is portrayed in the line drawing method, with thick and thin ink lines outlining the fullness and fluffiness of the feathers; the chick is dabbed in the ink halo method, with the moist ink blending naturally on the rice paper, and the different shades of ink rhyme revealing the chick's unformed feathers and awkward physique, demonstrating the artist's mastery of Chinese painting. The hazy hues of the lingering scene, if any, painted with light floral green add to the relaxed atmosphere and romantic poetry.
